title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Floatline Signals. Keep it, choose the field-guide alternative, take a challenger, or re-roll.

options.label: Floatline Signals
options.lineage: Cork floats, painted bite marks, and the line signals used by canal anglers
options.thesis: The float is not decoration; its changing depth tells the story of every fight.
options.viewport: The Village Canal fills the first screen, with Shallow Bank ready to fish, a visible float and line, a brief local-legend note, readable fight state, and a tactile CAST dock.
options.risk: A state instrument can crowd out the adventure; keep the living canal and fish larger than its readouts.

raised.raise: A rare catch reveals in stages: wake, fish, then collection record.

options.label: Freshwater Field Ledger
options.lineage: Regional fish survey plates and angler catch ledgers
options.thesis: Every catch becomes a useful, locally illustrated entry in the player's growing fish record.
options.viewport: Keep the canal scene dominant; a compact field label identifies the spot, the first-cast action is immediate, and the ledger edge previews discovery progress without hiding the water.
options.risk: Collection can become an encyclopedia instead of a game; live fishing must remain the first thing seen and done.

options.label: The Living Wake
options.lineage: Nocturnal plankton wakes and currents traced in living light
options.thesis: Water remembers the path of a fish just long enough for the player to read its next move.
options.viewport: A nighttime deep-water fight uses a bright wake to show fish direction while the player balances line tension and control.
options.case: Strongly dramatizes water, motion, and the King Fish; weaker as the common visual world for four varied canal spots and daylight play.
options.risk: A dark neon world can overwhelm Thai village life and the non-boss fish collection.

options.label: Canal Rumor Sheets
options.lineage: Photocopied village fishing-club notices and annotated rumor slips
options.thesis: The neighborhood's changing King Fish story is collected as marks, notes, and clues from the canal bank.
options.viewport: A broad playable canal view leads; clipped rumor notes, unlock stamps, and chapter clues live at its edge rather than replacing the fishing scene.
options.case: Fits the villagers' rumors and chapter progression, but the paste-up structure communicates narrative better than moment-to-moment fishing.
options.risk: Rough paper can read as urban punk rather than a peaceful rural game if carried too literally.

options.label: The Catch Reveal Tray
options.lineage: Darkroom test strips, timed development trays, and staged image reveals
options.thesis: A rare fish emerges in a deliberate reveal before it becomes a permanent collection record.
options.viewport: A caught fish reveals in three steps—wake, silhouette, full species and size—then resolves to its saved entry and reward.
options.case: The reveal ceremony fits rarity, but the darkroom has little connection to fishing, the canal, or the player's everyday journey.
options.kept: Use a short staged reveal for rare catches; keep the sequence legible and let the player proceed or skip it.
options.risk: A literal darkroom palette would make a peaceful outdoor fishing game feel enclosed and somber.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar polished fishing-game screen: scenic water, readable meters, spot selector, and clear action buttons.
canonCard.viewport: A large canal scene sits above a conventional row of location, progress, and fishing controls.
canonCard.risk: Easy to understand but easier to confuse with a standard game HUD; the signature fishing mechanic stays less distinctive.
